research_problem: API evolution research is large and scattered, hiding advances and remaining challenges
technical_approach: Systematic literature review (Kitchenham) with exact phrase 'API Evolution' across six libraries plus Google Scholar and snowballing; card sorting of topics and contribution types; extraction of goals, evaluations, subjects and challenges
primary_contribution: SLR of 369 API evolution studies (1994-2020) with trends, evaluation practices, state of the art and 17 existing + 15 unsolved challenges
evaluation_metrics: Descriptive counts and trends; test-retest reliability 0.94/0.97
key_findings: Publications more than doubled 2017-2018; maintenance 178 vs usability 161 papers; 63.9% evaluated only on Java; 74% of empirical studies lack statistical tests; many tools lack formal evaluation; non-standard metrics; key open challenges: drivers of API change, uniform benchmarks, cross-language impact, Web API tooling
author_limitations: Single search phrase; ad hoc taxonomy; incomplete coverage; selection/classification mostly by one author (test-retest checked)
analyst_limitations: Test-retest is not inter-rater agreement; inconsistent Java share (63.9/66/70.4%); library-centric search leaves Web/REST evolution nearly absent; no quality appraisal; cut-off 2020 excludes LLM era; preprint template version read
suggested_extensions: REST/OpenAPI evolution benchmark with breaking-change ground truth; cross-paradigm evolution comparison; LLM-era API evolution rapid review; ML prediction of change drivers; statistical-rigor meta-research
evidence_location: Method p.4-6; trends p.7-9; evaluation p.12-14; Java skew p.15; state of the art p.24-25; Table 7 p.28-29; threats p.31; conclusion p.32
integrity: Tables 1-5 column-split; trend figures missing; preprint DOI placeholder
